stem: What is the purpose of communication technologies, according to the lecture?

options.text: To empower users to send messages to each other

source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

stem: Which are the two main reasons digital communication is a good idea?

options.text: It enables the composition of modules into large systems
It allows sophisticated algorithms to improve quality and performance
Physical links are digital at the lowest level

explanation: Physical links are in fact analog at the lowest level.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

explanation: Each stage adds noise that cannot be removed.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

stem: How does a receiver recover the clock from the samples alone?

options.text: It infers a clock edge at every transition in the received samples
It asks the sender for the time
It counts the number of packets

explanation: It then extrapolates the other edges.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

stem: Which module maps bits to signals at the sender?
explanation: The demapper is its counterpart at the receiver.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

stem: Which is not one of the three abstractions used over each link?
explanation: The three are packets, bits and signals.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

stem: Physical communication links are digital at the lowest level.
explanation: They are analog, so data is converted between digital and analog.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1

stem: One problem in clock recovery is ensuring

options.text: that the sender has no clock

explanation: The other is coping with different clock frequencies.
source: CSC 222 Digital Communication lecture slides (Dr Adeniji Oluwashola David), Lecture 1
